check.title: Check a mod (static, nothing is run)
check.intro: Quick check skips the slow tools. Untick it for the full check (several minutes on a big mod).
check.speedH: How to make the check faster
check.speed1: Keep "Quick check" ticked while you work. Untick it for the full check before you share or release the mod.
check.speed2: A check of a mod whose files have not changed since the last full run is shown again from the store in about a second.
check.speed3: After you change a file, most checkers reuse what they kept about the files you did not change, so the next check is shorter than the first.
check.speed4: The first check of a mod is the slow one, and so is the first check after the cache folder was emptied. Do not let a cleaning tool empty %LOCALAPPDATA%\ARSENAL\cache.
check.speed5: Pack the mod into .pak files on an internal SSD: paks read much faster than thousands of loose files, for the check and for the game. Use the Share tab (Package for friends) and keep "Pack for speed" ticked (it is on by default): it sorts the files into one pak per kind, compresses only text and map .net and .grs files, stores the rest, and puts text first. A mod on a USB stick or a network share reads much more slowly.
check.speed6: Antivirus: add the mod folder and %LOCALAPPDATA%\ARSENAL\cache to the exclusions of real-time scanning; otherwise every file the check reads is scanned too.
check.speed7: The check uses every processor core: close other heavy programs while it runs.
check.speed8: In ARSENAL.exe each checker reads the mod on its own (the shared single read is not in the exe yet). Run from a source folder with Node.js (node tools/gui/gui.js for this window, node tools/as2/as2.js check <mod folder> for the command) and the checkers share one read of the mod, which is faster on a big mod.
fix.title: Fix: plan, then apply into a patch mod
fix.intro: Plan writes nothing. Apply writes a separate patch mod folder; the mod you chose is never changed.
fix.confirm: Write the patch mod folder now? Your mod is not changed.
up.title: Port to another target (upgrade)
up.intro: Preview first: it writes nothing. Write makes a new mod folder (out) and leaves yours alone.
up.confirm: Write the ported mod to the out folder?
ins.title: Install into the game
ins.intro: Copies the mod into the game mods folder (or links it). Dry shows what would happen.
ins.confirm: Copy the mod into the game mods folder?
rm.title: Remove an installed mod
rm.intro: Only removes a mod that as2 install put there. Type its folder name in the game mods folder.
rm.confirm: Remove this mod from the game mods folder?
ed.title: Test run in the editor build (pairs file)
ed.intro: It needs a pairs file. Pick the pairs in Unit pairs above and save them: the file is then filled in here. A dry run builds the mission into the out folder and starts no game. A real run starts the game for up to a few minutes and needs the server started with --allow-launch.
ed.confirm: This starts the game now. One game at a time; stop it with Cancel. Go?
pv.title: Prove one unit (plan only here)
pv.intro: Plan builds the fixture and scenario without a game. A real prove starts the game.
pv.confirm: This starts the game now. Go?
tr.title: Translate GoH units
tr.intro: With --donor, goh2as2 writes translated numbers. When a value is unusable or outside the AS2 range of its class, it asks and waits here: AS2 scale, the translated value, or the donor's own.
tr.noaskT: asking off: every case takes its default
tr.howT: Translate asks (--ask-json): one question per value, the page answers on the tool's stdin. "Translate, never ask" (--no-ask) takes every default (AS2 scale). Keys 1-3 pick, Enter takes the default, R ticks "rest of the class" (kept for that class and stage only).
x.scaleM: the GoH value mapped onto the range AS2 units of this class use
x.translatedM: the translation table's value, as it is
x.donorM: keep the donor unit's own value (nothing is written)
x.question: Question: {unit}  {key}  [{cls}, {stage}]
x.stage.engine: The translated value cannot be used by the engine (not a number, negative, or zero).
x.stage.scale: The translated value is outside what AS2 units of this class use.
x.l.transM: what the translation table gives for it
x.l.rangeM: 5th to 95th percentile of AS2 units of class {cls}
x.l.scaleM: the GoH value mapped into that range
x.rest: Apply to the rest of {cls} at this stage (R)
x.gone: the run is gone: nothing to answer
x.logq: ? {unit} {key} ({stage}): GoH {goh}, translated {tr}, AS2 scale {sc}, donor {donor}; default {def}
check.runT: Runs every static checker on the mod folder. Reads files only; nothing is written and the game is not started.
fix.planT: Shows what fix would change, without writing anything.
fix.applyT: Writes the fixes into the out folder (a new patch mod). Your mod folder is not changed.
wz.title: Guided fix: check the mod, see what is wrong, choose fixes
wz.intro: Seven steps. Each finding says what is wrong, where, why it matters and how to fix it. Automatic fixes are written to a NEW folder and never change your mod; fixes by hand are made in the Editor.
wz.adv: All options (advanced): the raw check and fix forms
wz.advT: Every option of check and fix, for when the guided steps are not enough.
wz.s1T: The mod folder to check. Choose it on the Mods screen; the chip at the top shows the current one.
wz.s2T: Runs the static checkers (reads files only, the game is not started), then plans the automatic fixes.
wz.s3T: One card per problem: what, where, why and how to fix.
wz.s4T: Tick the automatic fixes you want. Problems without an automatic fix keep their hand-fix steps.
wz.s5T: Writes only the ticked fixes into a new patch mod folder. The source mod is never written.
wz.s6T: The files that were written, what could not be fixed, and what to do next.
wz.s3H: Most serious first. Click a file name to see the lines around the problem.
wz.s4H: Safe fixes are ticked for you. Risky ones (they change how something looks) start unticked.
wz.s5H: The patch folder sits next to your mod by default. Enable it together with your mod in the game.
wz.changeT: Go to the Mods screen to pick another mod folder.
wz.fastT: Quick check skips the slow deep scans. Untick for the full check (slower, finds more, gives file names).
wz.noloadT: Leaves out the "would it load" pass (wouldload). Use it when that pass takes too long or never ends on this mod. There is then no load verdict.
wz.allgamesT: The load check reads only the game of this tab. Tick this to also check the other game builds (AS64, the original 32-bit game, Gates of Hell); they show as info only. Takes longer.
wz.restorepointsT: Restore points the tools keep inside the mod (the .arsenal-undo folder) are old copies the game never loads, so the check leaves them out. Tick this to check them too.
wz.auto: check again when the mod changes
wz.autoT: While this page is open, a change to the mod's files starts the check again a few seconds after the changes stop, at low priority, with the boxes as they are now. Needs the watch of the picked mod (Settings).
wz.autoOff: The watch of the picked mod is off (Settings), so the check does not run again by itself.
wz.autoErr: The mod folder cannot be watched ({m}), so the check does not run again by itself.
wz.checkT: Reads the mod and lists every problem found. Nothing is written.
wz.busy: Another run is going; wait for it or press Esc to cancel it.
wz.needGame: The game folder is not known: press "Game folder..." in the top bar. Fixes need it to compare with the game files.
wz.needPlan: No fix plan yet: the check has to finish first.
wz.safeOnlyT: Tick only fixes that do not change how anything looks or plays.
wz.partial: Fix applies whole groups: ticking part of {kinds} applies all of that group. The fix tool cannot pick single files yet.
wz.safeT: Only repairs references or text; nothing in the game looks different.
wz.riskyT: Changes how something looks (for example a stand-in material). Look at it in game after.
wz.outT: A NEW folder for the patch mod. It may not be inside your mod, hold your mod, or be inside the game folder (game/mods/<name> is allowed).
wz.outAbs: Use a full path (for example from Browse).
wz.outInMod: This is inside your mod. Pick a folder outside it: the source mod is never written.
wz.outHoldsMod: This folder holds your mod. Pick a new, separate folder.
wz.outInGame: Inside the game folder only game/mods/<name> is allowed.
wz.applyT: Writes the ticked fixes into the patch folder after you confirm.
wz.noWhere: No file location: the quick check of {tool} only counts. Untick quick check for file names.
wz.noWhereFull: No file location: {tool} names no file for this finding.
wz.manualNone: open the file and correct the line shown
wz.hitsCap: {k} of {n} places listed (check --locs N keeps more)
wz.toolReran: {tool} ran out of memory beside the other checkers and was rerun alone: its findings are complete.
wz.toolOom: {tool} ran out of memory, also when run alone ({m}). Its findings are missing.
wz.toolHint: Close other programs to free memory, then rerun only this checker.
wz.st.rerunTool: Running {tool} alone, one job. Nothing is written.
wz.st.rerunDone: {tool} rerun finished; its findings are shown.
wz.openT: Show the lines around this place in {p}
wz.editT: Open this file in the IDE at this line
wz.codeT: The checker's code for this problem. Search it with q.js -k CODE for more.
wz.tagT: [V] verified in game or code, [I] inferred, [T] needs an in-game test.
wz.limitsT: IDs in limits/ that describe this engine limit.
wz.autoRisky: Automatic fix: {fixer} (check the result in game).
wz.manualOnly: No automatic fix: follow the steps above by hand.
wz.verdictT: The overall verdict of this checker.
wz.noAuto: None of these problems has an automatic fix; use the hand-fix steps on each card.
wz.recheckT: Runs the check on your mod with the patch folder loaded on top, and compares counts.
wz.toTestT: Open Test, Share & Play > Test Run to test what the mod changed.
wz.toPlayT: Open Test, Share & Play > Play to try the mod in the game.
wz.revertedT: This change made things worse, so fix undid it.
wz.next2: Enable the patch mod {out} together with your mod, patch loaded after it.
wz.next3: Press Check again with the patch to see what is left.
wz.next4: Then open the Play page and press "Play a test match" before you share it.
wz.st.pick: Step 1: pick a mod on the Mods screen.
wz.st.ready: Ready: press Check the mod. It only reads files.
wz.st.checking: Checking the mod: reading its files with every checker. Nothing is written.
wz.st.auto: The mod changed: checking it again at low priority. Nothing is written.
wz.st.rechecking: Checking again with the patch {out} loaded on top.
wz.st.planning: {n} problem(s) found. Planning automatic fixes (nothing is written yet).
wz.st.review: {n} problem(s), {m} automatic fix(es) possible. Review the cards, then tick fixes.
wz.st.noGame: {n} problem(s) found. Press "Game folder..." in the top bar to plan fixes.
wz.st.done: Done: {n} file(s) written to {out}. See step 6.
wz.st.notrun: {cmd} did not start; see the log below.
adv.label: Advanced
adv.hint: Adds expert items and options inside the tabs you already have, such as Mods > Mod Files, Tools & Settings > Other Tools > Expert Tools and every upgrade setting on Upgrade or Port. It never adds a tab.
blk.switchT: Move, hide and show the parts of each page. Your arrangement is kept in a profile.
blk.onSay: Arrange is on. Each part of the page has a bar to move it or hide it. Press Esc or Done to finish.
blk.title: Arrange the page
blk.help: Drag a part by its handle, or use the buttons on its bar: the arrows move it up or down in its box, the box button moves it into the next box (with Shift: the box before), the cross hides it. The page's own controls do nothing while you arrange.
adv.chipT: Advanced is on. Open Settings to see what it adds or to turn it off.
adv.warn1: Advanced adds expert options inside the tabs you already have. It never adds a tab.
adv.warn2: Some of them write straight into mod files or start the editor build of the game.
adv.warn3: Keep a copy of your mod before you use them.
stg.lead: Settings for this window. Colours and language are in the top bar.
stg.mw.sw: Keep the file list of the picked mod up to date
stg.mw.p: While this window runs, it watches the folder of the picked mod (no admin rights needed) and lists it again a few seconds after files change. A check started here then takes that list instead of reading every file name of a big mod again. Off: every check lists the mod itself, and the Check page cannot check again by itself.
hd.lockT: Keep the header in view while scrolling
stg.adv.p: Advanced adds expert options inside the tabs you already have; it never adds a tab. Turning it on asks first.
stg.adv.folds: Folds marked Advanced inside pages, such as the expert options on Check
stg.adv.foldsU: Folds marked Advanced inside pages: every upgrade setting on Upgrade or Port, and the expert options on Check
stg.adv.kit: {p}: the Code Pieces that are not tried in game yet
stg.file: Your choices in this window are kept in {file}. Delete that file to reset the window.
stg.fileNone: Your choices in this window are kept only until ARSENAL closes this time.

nw.title: New blank mod (new)
nw.intro: Makes a blank AS64 mod folder: mod.info with MinGameVersion 3.301, a text file and a readme. Spaces in the folder name become _. Same as ARSENAL new.
pl.title: Play a test match (play)
pl.intro: Checks the mod, installs it, starts the game on a test map and reads game.log for the boot verdict. Dry run prints every step and changes nothing. Never uses game instance 0.
pl.confirm: This starts the game with your mod. Continue?
fl.dirT: The folder to make or use (full path).
fl.name: Name
fl.nameT: The name shown in the game Mods menu.
fl.descT: One line about the mod, shown in the Mods menu.
fl.depsT: Other mod folders this mod needs (Require lines).
fl.dryRunT: Shows what would be made and writes nothing.
fl.toT: Which game build the result is for.
fl.planT: Lists the changes and writes nothing.
fl.outT: A new folder for the result. Your mod is never changed.
fl.thenFixT: Runs the safe fixes on the result as well.
fl.as2T: The Men of War: Assault Squad 2 game folder.
fl.gohT: The Gates of Hell game folder (only read).
fl.withT: Other mods to check together with this one.
fl.exeT: Which exe to use (as64.exe or mowas_2.exe).
fl.gameT: Empty = the game folder in the top bar.
fl.fastT: Skips the slow checks. Good for big mods.
fl.noloadT: Leaves out the "would it load" pass. No load verdict then.
fl.allgamesT: Also checks the other game builds, not only the target game. Takes longer.
fl.restorepointsT: Also reads the restore points inside the mod (.arsenal-undo), which are left out by default.
fl.locsT: How many file:line places to keep per problem.
fl.modeT: Classic keeps the old look; Enhanced uses the AS64 features.
fl.linkT: Puts a link in the game mods folder instead of a copy.
fl.forceT: Replaces a folder that is already there.
fl.dryT: Shows the steps and changes nothing.
fl.yesT: Confirms the change without asking again.
fl.mapT: The map for the test match.
fl.instT: Which game copy (instance) runs the test.
fl.pairsT: A .json file that lists which unit shoots at which unit, for example my-pairs.json.
fl.unitT: The unit name as the game knows it.
fl.armyT: Which army the unit belongs to.
fl.donorT: The unit whose settings are copied.
fl.noDepsT: Does not copy the files the unit needs.
fl.askJsonT: The tool asks its questions as JSON (the page answers them).
fl.noAskT: Takes the default answer for every question.
fl.dropLimitsT: Removes values the game cannot use instead of stopping.
fl.noTranslateT: Copies the text without translating it.
hd.none: No verdict: the check gave no build result.
hd.good: Looks good for {b}: no crash class found.
hd.bad: Will probably crash or not load on {b}.
hd.mid: Loads on {b} with problems to look at.
hd.safeT: no crash problems found. Still play one test match first.
hd.notyetT: fix the problems below, then check again.
hd.noexe: The game build is not known: the game folder has no as64.exe or mowas_2.exe.
hd.nogame: Set the game folder (top bar) to get a verdict for your build.
hd.legendT: crash: the game may close or refuse the mod. silent: the game hides the mod or ignores a value without a message. review: check it yourself. info: only a note. LOADS_STATIC: no crash class found by reading the files; only a test match proves it works.
err.nomodinfo: This folder has no mod.info, so it is not a mod yet.
err.abs: Use a full path, for example C:\mods\my_mod.
err.makeT: Opens the New Mod card (AS64) or the Generator with this folder filled in.
game.on: game runs on for this session
mods.worksT: Which game build mod.info says the mod is for.
mods.inGameT: Is the mod in the game mods folder?
mods.healthT: The result of the last check on this PC.
mods.ro: Steam Workshop mod: only read. Upgrade or copy it to change it.
mods.where: Mods for the game live in: {p}
mods.emptyHere: No mods in these folders yet.

nw.dryDone: Preview done: nothing was written. Press the other button to make it.
nw.dryT: Shows what would be made, writes nothing. Same as: ARSENAL new <folder> --dry-run
nw.goT: Makes the mod folder. Same as: ARSENAL new <folder>
nw.badGoh: A GoH mod folder name may not have a '-' or letters outside plain ASCII (GoH does not load it).
nw.forG: For {g}: the mod.info is made for {g} (ARSENAL new --target {t}).
nw.forGoh: For {g}: the mod.info is made for {g} (ARSENAL new --target {t}); the folder name has no '-' and only plain ASCII letters.
na.upgrade.easy.goh: the easy card makes an AS64 copy of an old mod. For a GoH mod use the upgrade settings below (upgrade --to goh).
na.play.go.mowas2: a real test match needs instance 1 and the control pipe, and mowas_2.exe has no -console, -control or -instance (TST-19). Use the dry run; start the match in MoW:AS2 yourself.
na.play.tp.mowas2: the test game copy is the profile of instance 1, and mowas_2.exe has no -instance (TST-19).
na.test.edrun.mowas2: a real editor run needs its own instance profile and the control pipe, which MoW:AS2 does not have (TST-19). The dry run works.
na.test.prove.mowas2: a real prove run reads the game through the control pipe, which mowas_2.exe does not have (TST-19). The plan works.
na.test.edrun.goh: the GoH editor does not start the mission by itself, so ARSENAL cannot run the pairs. Save the pairs above and go through them in the game yourself.
na.test.prove.goh: a prove run reads the game through the control pipe, and GoH has no control pipe.
wz.outInGoh: ARSENAL writes into the GoH install only inside its mods folder: pick <GoH>/mods/<name> or a folder outside it.
mods.gohVer: GoH version {g}; mod.info range: Min {min}, Max {max}
mods.gohDev: GoH version {g}; Tags "develop": loads on any version (Min {min}, Max {max} are not checked)
smp.rename: give a unit a new name
smp.clone: copy a tank as a new unit
new.sampleT: Loads the chosen example into the box. Same as: ARSENAL gen --sample <name>
up.previewT: Lists the changes, writes nothing. Same as: ARSENAL upgrade <mod> --plan
up.writeT: Writes the upgraded copy to the out folder. Same as: ARSENAL upgrade <mod> --out <folder>
ub.title: Upgrade an old mod to AS64
ub.intro: Pick the old mod. A new folder next to it gets the upgraded copy; the old mod stays as it is.
ub.more: More settings come with Advanced: turn it on in Tools & Settings > Settings.
ub.modT: The mod folder to upgrade (a Workshop mod is fine: it is only read).
ub.modeT: Enhanced uses the AS64 features; Classic keeps the mod as close to the old one as it can.
ub.cls: Classic (as close to the old mod as possible)
ub.enhM: Enhanced: the mod runs only on AS64 and may use its new features.
ub.clsM: Classic: the mod keeps its old look and stays close to the original.
ub.previewT: Lists the changes, writes nothing. Same as: ARSENAL upgrade <mod> --to as64 --plan
ub.goT: Writes the upgraded copy to the new folder. Same as: ARSENAL upgrade <mod> --to as64 --out <folder>
ub.confirm: Write the AS64 copy of {mod} to {out}? The old mod is not changed.
ub.done: Done: the AS64 copy is in {p}. It is now the current mod.
ub.thenWrite: Nothing written yet. If the list looks right, press "Make the AS64 copy".
wz.fastSmall: Small mod ({n} files): the full check is used.
wz.fastBig: Big mod ({n} files): the quick check is used to save time.
wz.etaLong: taking longer than expected, still working
lc.title: Start the game from here

lc.off: Off: only previews run; the game is never started.
lc.confirm: Let ARSENAL start the game until you close this window? Save your other games first.

pe.s2: Puts the mod in the game mods folder (a marked copy or link).

pe.s4: Starts the game on the test map.
pe.s5: Puts your mod list back as it was.

pp.title: Unit pairs
pp.intro: Pick who shoots and who is shot at. ARSENAL fills in the crew, the distance and the rest. Leave Target empty and it picks a fitting target. Save the list and the test run below uses it.
pp.goh: Gates of Hell runs no test game here. The saved pairs file is still your list of what to try in the game.
pp.boxT: Type a unit id, a name from the game or an army. Pick a row and the id goes into the box.
pp.addT: The shooter fires at the target. This tests that the gun fires and does damage.
pp.revT: The target fires at the shooter. This tests that the shooter takes damage.
pp.needTarget: The reverse pair needs a target.
pp.noPair: The server sent no pair for these units.
pp.noRoute: Not ready on this server: {what} (the address answered 404). The rest of this card still works.
pp.r.describe: the sentence and the identifier of a pair
pp.idT: The identifier of this pair. It changes when the distance or a switch changes.
pp.distT: The distance between the two in metres. The pairs file holds map units, 20 for each metre.
pp.foeFireT: Off: the target holds its fire.
pp.watchT: The run records the hits, the broken parts and the health of the target.
pp.removeT: Takes this pair off the list.
pp.filterT: Shows the pairs whose identifier, unit name or unit id holds this text.
pp.empty: No pairs yet. Pick a shooter and press Add pair.
pp.checkT: Looks each pair over without a game: the units exist, the gun has ammunition, the distance fits.
pp.checkedBad: {m} of {n} pairs have a problem. See the note beside each.
pp.name: Name of the pairs file
pp.nameT: A short name. The file is kept with the test files of the mod.
pp.needName: Give the pairs file a name.
pp.needMod: Pick a mod first: pairs files are kept with the mod.
pp.saveT: Saves the list as a pairs file and puts its path into the test run below.
pp.saved: Saved {name}. The test run below now uses {path}.
pp.noSaved: No saved pairs files for this mod yet.
pp.loadT: Puts the pairs of this file into the list above.
pp.loadQ: Replace the list above with the pairs of {name}?
pp.delQ: Delete the saved pairs file {name}? This cannot be undone.
tr.who: Only for porting GoH units: it carries their numbers over to AS2 and asks you when a value does not fit.
fl.exportT: Leaves the UPGRADE.md report out and adds "Ported from X by Y" to the mod description. Only when writing, not in a preview.
cc.copyT: Shows the command line this form runs, for a terminal in the ARSENAL folder, and copies it.

gi.title: What is the Generator (gen)?
gi.what: gen builds a mod from one recipe file (a "spec"). The recipe lists changes; gen writes the unit files, the name text and the buy lists for you.
gi.when: For one unit the Units page is easier: it asks for each value. Use gen for many changes at once, to repeat them later, or to make the same changes for AS64, Classic and GoH.
gi.whenG: Use gen for many changes at once, to repeat them later, or to make the same changes for AS64, Classic and GoH.
gi.samples: The examples in the list below (pick one, press "{b}"):
gi.writes: Plan writes nothing and lists the files it would make. Write makes a new mod folder at the place shown in box 2; your other mods are not touched.
gi.gloss: What do spec, op and target mean?
gi.doc: Not the same as Bot Doctrine (Game Modes & AI > Bots > Bot Doctrine): that one picks a ready persona for how the computer player buys and fights.
tp.title: Test game copy (instance 1)
tp.intro: Play runs your mod in a separate copy of the game settings (instance 1), so your normal game and its mod list stay as they are. On a new PC this copy does not exist yet: look first, and make it if it is missing.
tp.lookT: Reads only: shows the mod list of instance 1.
tp.makeT: Copies your normal game settings into instance 1. Your normal game is not changed.
tp.confirm: Make the test game copy (instance 1)? Your normal game settings are copied into it; an older instance 1 copy is replaced. Your normal game is not changed.
tp.none: There is no test game copy yet. Press "Make the test game copy".
tp.ok: The test game copy exists. Play can use it.
tp.made: Done: the test game copy is made. Next: Play a test match > Dry run.
tp.fail: Could not read the test copy; see the lines below.
py.title: Use the mod in your normal game
py.s1: Install the mod (the Install card copies it into the game's mods folder).
py.s2: Start the game and open Options > Mods.
py.s3: Find your mod and move it to the Activated list.
py.s4: For an AS64 mod, keep as64+ in Activated, above your mod.
py.s5: Press Apply. "Applying mods..." shows for about 30 s; you do not restart the game. When Apply greys out it is done: close the dialog with X.
py.s6: Open a multiplayer or editor game and look for your change (buy panel, unit card).
py.note: Install only copies the folder; switching the mod on is done in the game. The test match above uses its own copy and does not need this.

rmt.title: LAN Remote
rmt.intro: Open this page on another device on the same home network: a phone, a tablet or another computer. The other device only looks; everything is changed here on the PC.
rmt.switch: Let another device on this network view the page
rmt.qr: QR code of the LAN Remote link
rmt.newLinkT: Make a new link. The old link and every device that used it stop working at once.
rmt.newSaid: New link made. The old link no longer works.
rmt.noLan: No network address found. Is this PC connected to a network?
rmt.onSay: On. Scan the code with the camera of the other device or open the link on it.
rmt.offSay: Off. Only this PC can open the page.
rmt.can: The other device can: see every page, open mods, read results, reports and files the PC page shows, follow the page the PC shows, and lead the PC page while Follow the remote device is on.
rmt.cannot: The other device cannot: run tools, save or change files, change settings, install, start the game or programs, or browse the folders of this PC.
rmt.fw: The first time, Windows may ask whether node may use the network. You answer that yourself; this tool never changes the firewall or system settings. Keep the link private: anyone with it on your network can look.
